papers.title: Objective motion-based performance assessment in STA-MCA microanastomosis: a postprocedural debriefing platform.
papers.abstract: The aim of this study was to develop and demonstrate a postprocedural motion analysis platform capable of objectively quantifying intraoperative surgeon micromovements to facilitate evidence-based self-debriefing in suturing superficial temporal artery-middle cerebral artery microanastomosis. The authors analyzed microscope-recorded microanastomoses performed by a cerebrovascular neurosurgeon. Seven suture-placement clips were extracted from operative videos. A computer vision tracking pipeline was implemented in Python using OpenCV to track the needle holder position across the video clips. Four motion metrics were computed for each video clip: absolute error, velocity, acceleration, and jerk. A unified reference distribution was constructed from all clips, and 95th percentile thresholds were defined for each metric. The metrics were displayed as dynamic synchronized plots alongside the corresponding video. Spectral decomposition of the position signal was performed to generate time-frequency representations, and average power in the 6- to 8-Hz band was computed as a quantitative tremor measure. To demonstrate reliable longitudinal performance tracking, the authors applied their platform to 8 recorded procedures between 2023 and 2026 and plotted the mean jerk per suture over time. Reliable tracking was achieved across 92.09% of analyzed footage. Two-dimensional trajectories were reconstructed for a total of 13,183 analyzed frames encompassing 219.82 seconds of suture-placement video (7 clips). Jerk analysis revealed multiple segments exceeding the 95th percentile threshold, flagging moments for surgical review. Time-frequency analysis revealed transient broadband power bursts and 2 persistent spectral bands (6-8 Hz and < 4 Hz). Tremor intensity analysis in the 6- to 8-Hz range revealed temporal tremor fluctuations, a finding undetectable by other metrics. Longitudinal performance tracking was feasible and demonstrated a stable jerk profile, consistent with expert-level performance. A motion-based postprocedural debriefing platform for the performance of microanastomosis is technically feasible and capable of generating objective, quantitative performance metrics from standard operative video. Unlike prior work focused on expert-novice differentiation, this platform was designed to support individualized self-assessment and reflective practice for surgeons at any experience level. Future work should validate the platform prospectively and correlate motion-based metrics with clinical outcomes.

papers.title: Machine Learning Classification of Bipolar Disorder Across Mood States Using Natural Language Processing and Speech Analysis: Observational Study.
papers.abstract: Bipolar disorder (BP) affects 1% to 3% of adults worldwide, with diagnostic delays averaging 6 years and high initial misdiagnosis rates. The absence of objective diagnostic measures contributes to clinical uncertainty and suboptimal outcomes. This study aimed to (1) develop a machine learning model for BP diagnosis and mood state classification using linguistic and acoustic features, (2) identify features associated with different mood states by comparing each with healthy controls (HC), and (3) explore whether features distinguish between mood states within BP. We analyzed data prospectively collected over 7 years from 61 patients with BP and 99 HC across Japan. Speech samples were collected via semistructured interviews over 1 to 5 visits and analyzed cross-sectionally, using aggregated or single-visit observations per participant rather than within-person longitudinal modeling. We extracted 6373 acoustic features (openSMILE 3.0, ComParE 2016) and 211 linguistic features. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO)-regularized logistic regression with nested cross-validation and age- and sex-matched undersampling was used. Mood states were classified as depressive state (DS; Hamilton Depression Rating Scale-17 [HAMD-17] ≥8, Young Mania Rating Scale [YMRS] ≤7), state with manic/mixed symptoms (MS/MX; YMRS ≥8), or euthymic state (ES; HAMD-17 ≤7, YMRS ≤7). Seven classification tasks included BP vs HC, each mood state vs HC, and interstate comparisons. Feature importance was validated via permutation testing (P<.05). Medication sensitivity analyses were performed. The model achieved high discrimination for BP vs HC (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC]=0.916, 95% CI 0.854-0.958; sensitivity 0.933; specificity 0.859) and strong performance for mood states vs HC (AUC=0.805-0.874). Acoustic features comprised 96% to 98% of the features achieving statistical significance (P<.05), including mel-frequency cepstral coefficients, spectral characteristics, and voice quality measures, showing strong correlations with diagnostic probabilities (|ρ|=0.35-0.85) and symptom severity (HAMD-17: ρ=-0.51; YMRS: ρ=-0.37); 2 to 4 linguistic features per comparison also reached significance. With sample independence ensured for interstate comparisons, DS vs ES significantly exceeded chance (AUC=0.760, permutation P=.03), whereas MS/MX vs ES (AUC=0.601, P=.20) and DS vs MS/MX (AUC=0.569, P=.30) did not, suggesting that markers primarily reflect persistent disease characteristics with partial state-associated components in depressive states. The combined acoustic-linguistic model, driven primarily by acoustic features, shows potential as an objective aid for BP diagnosis (AUC>0.9), largely free of medication confounding; some features remained detectable during euthymia, although ES discrimination could not be fully separated from concurrent antipsychotic treatment. Although DS showed partial distinguishability from ES, overall limitations remain for monitoring mood state changes. Findings require validation in diverse populations and against other psychiatric conditions.

papers.title: Reported Life-Threatening Polymorphic Ventricular Arrhythmia With Torsade-Like Morphology in a Patient With Gordon Syndrome and Hyperkalaemia.
papers.abstract: Gordon's syndrome (pseudohypoaldosteronism type II) is a rare, inherited tubulopathy characterised by salt-sensitive hypertension, hyperkalaemia, and metabolic acidosis despite preserved renal function. Pathogenic variants affecting the with-no-lysine (K) signalling pathway include WNK1, WNK4, KLHL3, and CUL3. We report the case of a 37-year-old woman with genetically confirmed CUL3-related Gordon's syndrome who developed hyperkalaemia after a three-week interruption of bendroflumethiazide. During pre-hospital assessment, ambulance clinicians documented a self-terminating rhythm that they identified as torsade de pointes. The original recording cannot be retrieved; consequently, the rhythm classification, preceding QT interval, and possible alternative rhythm or artefact could not be independently assessed. Point-of-care venous blood gas potassium was 4.8 mmol/L, whereas formal laboratory potassium was 6.1 mmol/L. The sampling and processing information available did not establish the cause of this discrepancy. Subsequent echocardiography, computed tomography coronary angiography, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, ambulatory monitoring, exercise testing, and additional electrical assessment did not identify a definitive alternative substrate, although an intermittent electrical disorder could not be excluded. Following treatment of hyperkalaemia and multidisciplinary cardiology and electrophysiology review, an extravascular implantable cardioverter-defibrillator was implanted. Bendroflumethiazide was resumed, with subsequent improvement in potassium control. This case highlights the importance of uninterrupted thiazide therapy in Gordon's syndrome, assessment of discordant potassium measurements, and careful interpretation of a reported serious rhythm event when its original tracing is unavailable. The temporal association with hyperkalaemia does not establish that it caused torsade de pointes.

papers.title: Clinical Symptom Burden and Its Association With Echocardiographic Parameters and Comorbidities in Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction: A Retrospective Study.
papers.abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a heterogeneous clinical syndrome in which substantial symptoms may occur despite preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). Echocardiographic abnormalities involving ventricular filling, left atrial remodeling, diastolic function, and pulmonary pressures may contribute to symptom burden. This study evaluated the association between clinical symptom severity, echocardiographic parameters, and comorbidities in patients with HFpEF. This retrospective observational cross-sectional study was conducted at the Government Peripheral Hospital, Periyar Nagar, Chennai, Tamil Nadu, from March 2025 to March 2026. A total of 216 patients aged ≥18 years with HFpEF and LVEF ≥50% were included. Clinical symptom burden was assessed using New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional class and categorized as I-II or III-IV. Demographic characteristics, comorbidities, and echocardiographic parameters, including LVEF, left ventricular mass, left atrial volume index (LAVI), E/e' ratio, diastolic dysfunction grade, and estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure (PASP), were evaluated. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors independently associated with NYHA III-IV symptoms. The mean age was 67.8 ± 10.4 years, and 53.7% were female. Hypertension was the most prevalent comorbidity (80.6%), while 76.9% had ≥2 major comorbidities. Fifty-five patients (25.5%) had NYHA III-IV symptoms. Compared with NYHA I-II, the severe symptom group had higher E/e' (17.4 ± 5.0 vs. 12.6 ± 4.0), LAVI (44.5 ± 12.1 vs. 34.2 ± 9.1 mL/m²), LV mass, and PASP (43.9 ± 12.4 vs. 36.8 ± 8.7 mmHg), with significantly more advanced diastolic dysfunction. On multivariable analysis, E/e' (adjusted OR 1.18), LAVI (adjusted OR 1.05), and PASP (adjusted OR 1.04) were independently associated with severe symptoms. Symptom severity in HFpEF was associated more strongly with abnormal filling pressures, left atrial remodeling, and pulmonary hemodynamics than with preserved systolic function alone. E/e', LAVI, and PASP may provide useful complementary markers of symptomatic burden and support a multidimensional echocardiographic assessment of HFpEF.

papers.title: Effect of Preoperative Intranasal Dexmedetomidine on Postoperative Myocardial Injury in Patients Undergoing Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting.
papers.abstract: To evaluate the effects of preoperative intranasal dexmedetomidine on postoperative myocardial injury biomarkers in patients undergoing on-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). In this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 70 patients undergoing on-pump CABG were assigned to receive intranasal dexmedetomidine (1 μg/kg) or saline 30 min before bedtime on the night before surgery and again 30 min before anesthesia induction. The primary outcome was serum high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T (hs-cTnT) at 24 h after surgery. Secondary outcomes included perioperative cardiac biomarkers, preoperative sleep quality, postoperative delirium, and adverse events. For the prespecified primary outcome, hs-cTnT concentrations at 24 h after surgery were significantly lower in the dexmedetomidine group than in the control group (estimated marginal means, 170.29 vs 357.29 ng/L; P < 0.001). Postoperative creatine kinase-MB (CK-MB) concentrations were also lower in the dexmedetomidine group (all P < 0.05). N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide showed a significant group-by-time interaction (P = 0.030), although between-group differences at individual postoperative time points were not significant. The dexmedetomidine group had higher Leeds Sleep Evaluation Questionnaire scores (62 [60-64] vs 44 [41-50]; P < 0.001) and a lower incidence of postoperative delirium (14.3% vs 37.1%; P = 0.029). Adverse events, mechanical ventilation duration, and intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay did not differ significantly between groups. In this single-center trial, two-dose preoperative intranasal dexmedetomidine was associated with lower postoperative hs-cTnT and CK-MB concentrations, better subjective preoperative sleep quality, and a lower observed incidence of postoperative delirium. These findings are preliminary and require confirmation in larger, adequately powered multicenter randomized trials to determine whether the biomarker reductions translate into clinically meaningful cardiovascular benefits. papers.title: Avoiding Diagnostic Pitfalls in Facial Pain: A Case Report of Paroxysmal Hemicrania Initially Treated as Trigeminal Neuralgia.
papers.abstract: A 21-year-old man presented with a two-year history of recurrent, strictly unilateral left-sided pain in the upper maxillary and orbital regions, radiating to the temporal and occipital areas. Individual attacks lasted 20 to 30 minutes and occurred 10 to 20 times daily, on most days throughout the two-year period. He had been diagnosed elsewhere with trigeminal neuralgia and treated with carbamazepine 200 mg twice daily without benefit. He denied photophobia, phonophobia, and ipsilateral cranial autonomic features, but described prominent restlessness during attacks. No cutaneous or mucosal trigger could be identified, and neurological examination was normal. The attack duration, the reported high attack frequency, the absence of tactile triggers, and the restlessness were inconsistent with classical trigeminal neuralgia and raised suspicion of a trigeminal autonomic cephalalgia, including probable paroxysmal hemicrania. Carbamazepine was withdrawn, and an escalating oral indomethacin trial was initiated, reaching 225 mg daily and maintained at that dose for 14 consecutive days. A headache diary begun on the first day of the trial recorded headache on all 20 days, and the patient reported no improvement at any point. Because the phenotype fulfilled all but the indomethacin-response criterion, the diagnosis was recorded as probable paroxysmal hemicrania, while cluster headache and other trigeminal autonomic cephalalgias remained in the differential diagnosis. Verapamil 240 mg daily was substituted on day 21. Headache days fell to 23 of 31 in the first month and 13 of 31 in the second, with the last 18 days of the second month free of headache. At telephone follow-up, the patient reported sustained resolution, with only mild headaches related to sleep deprivation that he considered distinct from his previous syndrome. He remains on verapamil. Whether verapamil produced the improvement cannot be established from a single uncontrolled case, as the drug was never withdrawn, and spontaneous remission remains possible. This case illustrates the clinical overlap between trigeminal neuralgia and the trigeminal autonomic cephalalgias and highlights the value of structured longitudinal symptom recording, ideally including individual attack count, duration, autonomic features, and triggers.

papers.title: First-year changes in mental health, lifestyle behaviors, and social support among international students at a Japanese university.
papers.abstract: International students experience psychological distress due to cultural adjustment, loneliness, and limited social support. However, longitudinal evidence remains scarce in Japan, and comprehensive models incorporating lifestyle and social factors remain underexamined. This study investigated the changes in mental health symptoms, lifestyle behaviors, and social support during international students' first year after university enrollment. Furthermore, we examined longitudinal changes and their associations with academic year repetition. This study included 216 international students who enrolled between 2016 and 2024. They completed questionnaire surveys upon university enrollment and 1 year later. Measures included the Kessler Psychological Distress Scale (K6), suicidal ideation, interpersonal tension, sleep duration, and number of available social supporters. Changes from baseline to 1-year later were examined. Univariable logistic regression analyses were performed with academic year repetition as the outcome and baseline variables and variables that changed as predictors. Of the participants, 1.9% exhibited severe psychological distress (K6 ≥ 13 points) and 15.9% reported suicidal ideation at enrollment. Psychological distress did not significantly change over the first year. However, significant changes were observed in both weekend sleep duration (χ 2 = 28.452, p < 0.001) and weekday sleep duration (χ 2 = 6.838, p = 0.033), fewer available supporters (Z = 2.757, p = 0.006), and reduced interpersonal tension (Z = 2.549, p = 0.011). Furthermore, an increase in weekend sleep duration was associated with academic year repetition (odds ratio [OR] = 3.131, p = 0.027). Reduced interpersonal tension exhibited a trend toward lower repetition risk (OR = 0.131, p = 0.052). Monitoring changes in sleep duration and interpersonal tension after enrollment may enhance academic and mental health support for international students.

papers.title: Effect of Adding Esketamine to Patient-Controlled Intravenous Analgesia on Rebound Pain After Interscalene Brachial Plexus Block: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.abstract: Rebound pain after peripheral nerve block (PNB) may diminish the analgesic benefits of regional anesthesia. Whether esketamine administered via postoperative patient-controlled intravenous analgesia (PCIA) can prevent rebound pain remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of esketamine-containing PCIA on rebound pain after interscalene brachial plexus block in patients undergoing shoulder arthroscopic surgery. 132 patients scheduled for arthroscopic shoulder surgery under general anesthesia combined with interscalene brachial plexus block were randomized 1:1 to receive postoperative PCIA with esketamine (1.25 mg/kg) plus sufentanil (100 μg) and flurbiprofen axetil (100 mg) (ES group, n=66) or sufentanil plus flurbiprofen axetil alone (Control group, n=66). The primary outcome was rebound pain, defined as an increase from well-controlled pain (NRS ≤ 3) to severe pain (NRS ≥ 7), typically after resolution of the nerve block. Secondary outcomes included time to rebound pain, modified pain score, rebound pain duration, analgesic consumption, numerical rating scale (NRS) at 6, 12, 24, and 48 h postoperatively, Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15), Richards-Campbell Sleep Questionnaire (RCSQ) sleep quality, and adverse events. The incidence of rebound pain did not differ significantly between groups (25.8% vs 39.4%; OR, 0.53; 95% CI, 0.39 to 1.09; P=0.095). Among patients who developed rebound pain, the ES group had a lower modified rebound pain score and shorter pain duration. For other secondary outcomes, patients receiving esketamine had lower NRS pain scores at 12, 24, and 48 h, fewer PCIA demands, less rescue analgesic use, and higher QoR-15 and RCSQ scores (all P<0.05). The incidence of the assessed adverse events did not differ significantly between groups. Adding esketamine to postoperative PCIA did not demonstrate a reduction in rebound pain incidence after interscalene brachial plexus block. Exploratory subgroup findings suggested lower rebound pain intensity and duration, while improvements in postoperative analgesia, sleep, and recovery had uncertain clinical relevance. Further multicenter studies are needed to confirm these findings and to evaluate different dosing strategies and routes of administration.

papers.title: Esketamine as a Perineural Adjuvant to Ropivacaine for Pericapsular Nerve Group (PENG) Block in Elderly Patients Undergoing Hip Fracture Surgery: A Propensity Score-Matched Retrospective Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: Hip fractures are increasing with global aging. We evaluated esketamine as a perineural ropivacaine adjuvant for PENG block on early recovery quality and analgesia in elderly hip fracture surgery patients. In this retrospective cohort study (July 2024-May 2025), 252 elderly patients undergoing hip fracture surgery under general anesthesia were included. Patients were allocated to control or esketamine groups based on adjuvant use. Propensity score matching yielded 86 pairs. The primary outcome was QoR-15 scores at multiple postoperative time points; secondary outcomes included sensory block duration, sleep quality, pain scores, and adverse events. At 24 and 48 hours, QoR-15 scores were higher with esketamine (median difference, 9 [95% CI, 7-11] and 4 [95% CI, 2-6]). Sensory block was prolonged (16.51 ± 1.30 vs 10.91 ± 1.26 hours; P <0.001). On day 1, sleep quality and VAS pain scores improved (both P <0.001), but neither difference exceeded the population-specific MCID. Time to first ambulation was shorter, and intraoperative propofol and remifentanil use was lower (both P <0.001). Frailty, age, anxiety, and higher aCCI predicted unfavorable recovery trajectories. Among elderly patients undergoing hip fracture surgery, esketamine added to ropivacaine for PENG block improved 24-hour recovery quality (QoR-15, exceeding MCID; 48-hour scores higher but below MCID), prolonged sensory block, shortened time to first ambulation, and reduced intraoperative anesthetic and opioid use. Sleep and analgesia improved only at 24 hours but did not exceed population-specific MCIDs. No difference in adverse events was detected within sample size constraints. In an exploratory latent trajectory analysis of the control group, frailty, age, anxiety, and aCCI predicted poor recovery.

papers.title: Mood and Behavioral Changes in Adult Cerebral X-linked Adrenoleukodystrophy.
papers.abstract: A 33-year-old man with genetically confirmed X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy developed progressive irritability, emotional lability, anger outbursts, repetitive reassurance-seeking, and insomnia alongside worsening spastic paraparesis and urinary symptoms. Difficulty recalling familiar names and remembering and completing assigned tasks subsequently impaired occupational functioning. Collateral history established a departure from his calm and socially appropriate premorbid personality. Behavioral examination revealed overfamiliarity, disinhibited language, emotional lability, impaired judgment, and perseverative illness-related preoccupation. Cognitive examination demonstrated impaired attention, set-shifting, verbal fluency, inhibitory control, new learning, and recent recall, while neurological examination revealed pyramidal signs and a spastic gait. Brain magnetic resonance imaging showed symmetrical posterior cerebral white-matter hyperintensities, and genetic testing identified an ABCD1 c.323C>A variant. The temporal association with neurological progression, acquired behavioral change, cognitive impairment, and characteristic imaging abnormalities supported secondary mood syndrome with accompanying behavioral and cognitive manifestations rather than a primary depressive episode or adjustment disorder. Irritability, sleep, and anger outbursts improved during approximately one week of inpatient treatment with supportive intervention, low-dose quetiapine, and sodium valproate, although post-discharge follow-up was unavailable. This case emphasizes that new affective, behavioral, or cognitive symptoms in cerebral white-matter disease should prompt collateral history-taking, cognitive and neurological examination, and reassessment for disease progression.

papers.title: Perceptual lengthening of visual time throughout learning of hand-reaching actions.
papers.abstract: Timing is intimately woven into human cognition and behavior, yet the dynamic interplay between timing and action remains poorly understood, particularly during goal-directed action learning. Using combined behavioral, electroencephalographic, and modeling approaches, we investigated how perceptual time changes as participants gained experience in a goal-directed reaching task requiring different degrees of action planning. Participants judged brief visual durations while preparing hand movements toward visual targets. Subjective time expanded during action preparation, which gradually increased across trials mirroring gradual improvements in action readiness. Representational similarity analysis revealed dissociable neural responses linking action and timing: action planning influenced time encoding during timed stimulus presentation, whereas broader motor engagement shaped subsequent time decoding following stimulus presentation. These findings extend previous accounts of action-dependent changes in perceived time, showing that the interaction is dynamic, evolving with changes in action readiness, and is mediated by dissociable neural responses during time encoding and decoding stages.

papers.title: Prevalence of Sleep Disorders in Patients With Knee, Hip, and Hand Osteoarthritis: A Systematic Review With Meta-Analysis.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To estimate the pooled prevalences of insomnia, obstructive sleep apnea, restless legs syndrome, and narcolepsy in patients with knee, hip, or hand osteoarthritis. DESIGN: Prevalence systematic review with meta-analyses. The review protocol was preregistered at PROSPERO (CRD420251005836). LITERATURE SEARCH: We conducted systematic searches in Embase, MEDLINE, and the Cochrane Library from inception to August 2025, supplemented by citation screening and reference checking. STUDY SELECTION CRITERIA: We identified observational and interventional studies reporting prevalence data on sleep disorders among patients with knee, hip, or hand osteoarthritis. DATA SYNTHESIS: Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation tool. Pooled prevalence estimates were calculated using random-effects proportion meta-analyses, with subgroup analyses based on diagnostic criteria and patient characteristics. RESULTS: Eighteen studies (202 847 participants) were included (three cohort, five case-control, 12 cross-sectional), of which nine studies were of very good to good or high quality. Insomnia was the most prevalent sleep disorder, 42% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 34% to 51%), followed by sleep apnea (37% [95% CI: 6% to 67%]) and restless legs syndrome (35% [95% CI: 10% to 61%]). No studies reported on narcolepsy. Estimates varied by diagnostic criteria and sample characteristics across studies, and the certainty of evidence was very low. CONCLUSION: Sleep disorders, particularly insomnia, were common among patients with knee, hip, or hand osteoarthritis, supporting the need to raise clinical awareness. Future studies may alter prevalence estimates, as only a small number of high-quality studies were identified and large between-study heterogeneity was observed. papers.title: Sleep architecture disruption and coordinated patterns of inflammatory and extracellular matrix biomarkers in obstructive sleep apnea: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the associations between circulating inflammatory, extracellular matrix (ECM), and oxidative stress biomarkers and polysomnographic parameters across different severity levels of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), with adjustment for body mass index (BMI). Seventy adults with confirmed OSA were categorized as mild-to-moderate or severe based on apnea-hypopnea index (AHI). Serum levels of TNF-α, IL-6, MMP-2, MMP-9, desmosine, cellular fibronectin (cFN), syndecan-1 (SDC-1), glutathione (GSH), and malondialdehyde (MDA) were measured using ELISA or spectrophotometric methods. Biomarker concentrations were natural-log transformed to satisfy normality assumptions; between-group comparisons were adjusted for BMI using ANCOVA. Associations among biomarkers and clinical variables were assessed using Spearman correlation, BMI-adjusted partial correlation, and network analysis. Severe OSA was associated with higher levels of TNF-α, IL-6, MMP-2, MMP-9, desmosine, and cFN compared with mild-to-moderate OSA (all p < 0.05). SDC-1 reached statistical significance after BMI adjustment (p = 0.009). These biomarkers were positively associated with AHI, oxygen desaturation index (ODI), desaturation count, and time spent with SpO₂ <90% (T90), and inversely associated with N3 sleep duration. After adjustment for BMI, strong inter-biomarker partial correlations (r = 0.831-0.921, p < 0.001) formed a densely connected inflammatory-ECM cluster; this pattern remained significant, albeit more modest in magnitude, in sensitivity analyses using unadjusted Spearman correlations (ρ = 0.427-0.655, p < 0.001). GSH and MDA showed weaker and more isolated associations. OSA severity is associated with coordinated patterns among inflammatory and ECM-related biomarkers that parallel hypoxic burden and sleep architecture changes. In contrast, systemic oxidative stress markers appear less integrated within these patterns. These findings support the potential utility of multi-biomarker approaches in reflecting disease-related physiological alterations, potentially arising from both systemic and local upper airway tissue processes.

papers.title: Lived experiences and quality of life in people with severe, biologic-treated chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps: a hermeneutic phenomenological study.
papers.abstract: Chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) is an inflammatory disease that affects quality of life. Diagnostic delays, symptom recurrence, and treatment failure increase the uncertainty and frustration of those affected. The objective of this study was to retrospectively explore the lived experiences of people with severe, biologic-treated CRSwNP from the onset of symptoms through to the failure of both appropriate medical therapy and surgery, in relation to the impact of the disease on their quality of life. A qualitative study based on Gadamer's hermeneutics was conducted. Between April 2024 and April 2025, 16 adults with severe biologic-treated CRSwNP participated in the study. They were selected through purposive sampling in a single airway clinic. Medical history was taken, nasal examination was performed, and imaging tests were undertaken, followed by in-depth interviews. Data were interpreted following a Gadamerian hermeneutic-circle approach, operationalised through Fleming's method. Three main themes were developed: (1) the silent burden of symptoms and their impact on daily life; (2) the odyssey to obtain a diagnosis; and (3) the experience of treatment failure and the associated emotional strain. People with severe, biologic-treated CRSwNP experience communication and sleep difficulties, impaired sex life, discrimination and self-medication, which substantially deteriorates their quality of life. This is compounded by diagnostic uncertainty, the need for self-management, treatment failure, and the ongoing search for information. Family support has a meaningful impact on their biopsychosocial well-being. These findings illustrate how physical, emotional and social dimensions are intertwined throughout this disease trajectory.

papers.title: Nasal symptoms are independently associated with subjective sleep impairment and symptom awareness in obstructive sleep apnea: an otolaryngology-based cohort study.
papers.abstract: Nasal disorders are common in obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). We previously reported an association between nasal symptoms and impaired sleep in non-obese OSA patients without multivariate adjustment. This study examined whether nasal symptoms are independently associated with subjective sleep quality and characterized the discordance phenotype in an otolaryngology-based cohort. This retrospective study included 628 OSA patients (AHI ≥ 5 events/h). Nasal symptoms were assessed using the JRQLQ. Sleep quality was measured by the ESS, AIS, and PSQI. Discordance was defined as AHI ≥ 30 events/h with absent subjective impairment (ESS ≤ 10, AIS ≤ 5, or PSQI ≤ 5). All questionnaire scores worsened with nasal symptom severity (all p < 0.001), whereas polysomnographic parameters did not differ. Nasal symptom score was independently associated with ESS ≥ 11 (OR 1.159), AIS ≥ 6 (OR 1.163), and PSQI ≥ 6 (OR 1.247; all p < 0.001); AHI was non-significant. Nasal obstruction retained significance for AIS ≥ 6 and PSQI ≥ 6 after adjustment. Objective nasal resistance did not correlate with symptoms (r = - 0.022). Discordance was present in 63.0% by ESS, rising to 90.3% at age ≥ 75 years. Nasal symptom score was associated with discordance across all definitions (OR 0.755-0.871; all p ≤ 0.027); AHI was non-significant. Nasal symptoms are independently associated with subjective sleep impairment in OSA beyond polysomnography-defined severity. Daytime rhinomanometry does not reflect nasal symptoms or sleep quality. Most patients with severe OSA lacked perceived impairment; nasal symptom burden was the only factor consistently associated with discordance. Multidimensional nasal and sleep assessment is recommended.

papers.title: Neurodevelopmental outcomes of infants evaluated for but not treated with therapeutic hypothermia: a prospective cohort study.
papers.abstract: Therapeutic hypothermia (TH) is the standard of care for moderate to severe neonatal encephalopathy (NE). Although some centers consider TH for mild NE, neurodevelopmental outcomes of infants who do not meet eligibility criteria are incompletely defined. Infants evaluated for TH based on perinatal risk factors, but who did not meet institutional eligibility criteria, were prospectively enrolled. Neurodevelopmental outcomes were assessed at 24 months. Bayley-4 scores <85 were classified as sub-normative performance. Of 39 infants enrolled, 26 completed Bayley-4 assessments. Thirteen (50%) demonstrated sub-normative performance in at least one developmental domain; only one of them had an acute brain injury on MRI. Compared with infants with average-range performance, those with sub-normative performance had higher postnatal base deficits (10.1 vs 6 mmol/L, p 0.04), higher postnatal lactate levels (9.4 vs 4.9 mmol/L, p 0.05), and a trend toward less sleep-wake cycling on aEEG (45% vs 83%, p 0.06). A substantial proportion of infants evaluated for but not treated with TH demonstrated sub-normative developmental performance at 2 years. Absence of acute MRI-detected injury does not preclude later developmental vulnerability. These findings support longitudinal follow-up of infants who are evaluated for TH but do not meet TH criteria. Infants evaluated for but not treated with therapeutic hypothermia demonstrated a measurable risk of neurodevelopmental vulnerability at 2 years, with 50% demonstrating sub-normative performance (>1 SD below the normative mean) in at least one domain on the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development Fourth Edition. Early postnatal metabolic abnormalities in infants evaluated for therapeutic hypothermia showed a potential association with later developmental outcomes. There is a need for improved risk stratification and structured longitudinal follow-up for infants evaluated for but who do not meet cooling criteria.

papers.title: Predictors of delayed discharge after adolescent metabolic and bariatric surgery.
papers.abstract: Enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) protocols have shortened hospital stays following metabolic and bariatric surgery (MBS); however, a subset of adolescents still experience delayed discharge, and contemporary national data remain limited. Evaluate the incidence, temporal trends, and predictors of delayed discharge following adolescent MBS. Multicenter, national database study. Retrospective cohort study utilizing the 2015-2024 Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery Accreditation and Quality Improvement Program (MBSAQIP) database. Adolescents (ages 10 to <20) undergoing primary minimally invasive vertical sleeve gastrectomy (SG) or Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) were included. Delayed discharge was defined as postoperative length of stay (LOS) >2 days. Temporal trends were assessed with Cochran-Armitage test. Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of delayed discharge. Among the 10,553 adolescents (85.9% SG, 14.1% RYGB), delayed discharge occurred in 713 (6.8%) patients and was more common after RYGB than SG (9.6% vs 6.3%, P < .001). Delayed discharge decreased significantly over the study period for both procedures (both P < .001). Independent predictors of delayed discharge included Asian race (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 5.15; 95% confidence interval [CI], 3.11-8.22), Hispanic ethnicity (aOR, 1.83; 1.48-2.25), sleep apnea (aOR, 1.56; 1.26-1.94), and Black race (aOR, 1.34; 1.08-1.67). Robotic approach (aOR, .54; .36-.78), increasing age (aOR, .88/yr; .83-.93), and operative year (aOR, .89/yr; .86-.92) were associated with decreased odds of delayed discharge. Delayed discharge after adolescent MBS is uncommon and declining. Several modifiable and nonmodifiable predictors were identified that inform preoperative risk stratification, targeted perioperative optimization, and discharge planning in this population.

papers.title: Temporal Eating Patterns Show Inconsistent Associations With Cancer Incidence and Mortality: Systematic Review of Prospective Studies.
papers.abstract: Temporal eating patterns, such as eating time, frequency, and regularity, may be associated with cancer outcomes through circadian and metabolic pathways, but evidence remains limited. We aimed to systematically review prospective studies examining associations between temporal eating patterns and cancer incidence or mortality. Following PRISMA guidelines, PubMed and Embase were searched from inception to September 2, 2026. Eligible studies included prospective cohorts of adults assessing eating or fasting duration, nighttime eating, breakfast frequency or timing, meal regularity, or eating frequency in relation to cancer incidence or mortality. Meta-analyses were conducted when ≥3 studies examined comparable exposure-outcome pairs, and the quality of meta-evidence was evaluated using the NutriGrade scoring system. Risk of bias was assessed using the Risk of Bias for Nutrition Observational Studies tool. Seventeen prospective cohort studies were included. Findings for eating or fasting duration and nighttime eating varied across studies for both cancer incidence and mortality. Lower breakfast frequency was associated with higher cancer mortality and colorectal cancer incidence in some studies, but not with breast cancer incidence. Greater eating-time variability and unrestrained eating were associated with higher cancer mortality, with unrestrained eating also associated with higher colorectal cancer incidence. Associations between eating frequency and cancer outcomes varied across studies and cancer sites. A meta-analysis of three studies showed a non-significant inverse association between eating frequency and colorectal cancer incidence in both categorical (HR = 0.81, 95% CI: 0.64-1.03) and dose-response analyses (HR per 1 time/day increase = 0.95, 95% CI: 0.89-1.01), with very low-quality meta-evidence. Risk of bias varied across domains, with common concerns related to confounding and exposure changes over follow-up. Findings from cohort studies suggest potential associations between temporal eating patterns and cancer outcomes, but the evidence remains limited and heterogeneous, underscoring the need for further investigation. papers.title: Reduced Locomotor Activity in Juvenile ICR and BALB/c Mice Exposed to Early-Life Sleep Restriction.
papers.abstract: Sleep during early life is essential for normal brain development, and its disruption is implicated as a risk factor for later behavioral abnormalities. We previously reported that chronic postnatal sleep restriction in C57BL/6N mice impairs parvalbumin interneuron development and produces anxiety-like behavior and persistent reductions in locomotor activity into adulthood. Whether these behavioral consequences extend to other genetic backgrounds remains unclear. Here, male ICR (outbred) and BALB/c (inbred) mice underwent daily sleep restriction by gentle handling from postnatal day 8 to 21, and body weight, open-field behavior, and social interaction were assessed thereafter; body weight and open-field behavior were reassessed at 8 weeks of age following return to standard housing. During the juvenile period, sleep restriction reduced total distance traveled in the open field in both strains, without a significant strain × treatment interaction. Significant interactions were found for body weight and time in the central area, both of which were altered in ICR but not in BALB/c mice. In the social interaction test, sleep restriction reduced locomotion and the number of contacts in both strains. At 8 weeks of age, the reduction in total distance traveled remained detectable across strains, and no other measure was affected. BALB/c mice differed from ICR mice in most measures irrespective of treatment. These findings indicate that early-life sleep restriction reduces locomotor activity in both strains, whereas its effects on body weight and central-area exploration were strain-specific. Because sleep was not directly measured and restriction relied on gentle handling, contributions of handling stress cannot be excluded.

papers.title: Age-related patterns in local spontaneous activity measured by fNIRS: greater unpredictability in infancy, local reorganization in childhood.
papers.abstract: The maturation of the brain is typically described at the whole-brain scale, whereas age-related changes in spontaneous activity within local brain regions have received comparatively little attention. Resting-state regional dynamics (RSRD) are defined as the temporal variability characteristics of activity within a single brain region under the resting state, and can stably reflect the intrinsic properties of spontaneous brain activity. The present study compared two age periods: infants (1-8 months of age) recorded during natural sleep and children (4-15 years of age) recorded during wakeful rest, corresponding to distinct developmental stages of rapid postnatal structural and functional brain development. The results suggested markedly different age-related feature patterns between the two groups: during infancy the predominant change was an increase in unpredictability, with RSRD activity becoming increasingly complex, whereas during childhood the dominant feature was a systematic reorganization of local waveform patterns. Age-related RSRD changes in the prefrontal cortex suggested a linear trend in infancy and a mixed linear-nonlinear trend in childhood, with inter-regional differences in the magnitude of feature changes. Vascular maturation-related indices suggested an association with RSRD feature changes during infancy, but not during childhood, suggesting that vascular factors may play a relatively more prominent role in early developmental stages. External data and exploratory internal cross-validation provided preliminary support for the age-related nature of these features, although further validation in larger, independent cohorts is needed.

papers.title: Brain metabolomics reveals metabolic alterations associated with chronic polystyrene microplastic-induced neurotoxicity in Drosophila melanogaster.
papers.abstract: Microplastic (MP) pollution is a widespread global environmental problem and poses growing risks to food safety and human health. Increasing evidence indicates that MPs accumulate in human biological tissues, including the brain. However, the brain-specific metabolic alterations associated with chronic MPs exposure remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the neurotoxic effects of chronic dietary exposure to polystyrene microplastics (PS-MPs; 10 and 50 ppm) in Drosophila melanogaster using an integrated metabolomic, biochemical, histological, and behavioral approach. Chronic dietary exposure to PS-MPs is linked to behavioral impairments, including decreased locomotor activity, impaired climbing, altered feeding, and reduced circadian amplitude, at the two tested concentrations. Untargeted brain metabolomics revealed widespread alterations in amino acid, nitrogen, kynurenine, polyamine, and central carbon metabolism, including reduced putrescine, elevated spermidine and spermine, and perturbations in glycolytic and tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle intermediates. Biochemical analyses demonstrated elevated oxidative stress and impaired antioxidant defenses, including reduced catalase (↓46%) and superoxide dismutase (↓40%) activity, and evidence of mitochondrial impairment (increased mitochondrial ROS, loss of membrane potential, reduced electron transport, altered NAD/NADH balance, and diminished metabolic viability). Histological examination revealed increased brain tissue damage and decreased neuronal viability. Moreover, PS-MPs exposure was associated with alterations in dopaminergic markers, including reduced tyrosine hydroxylase and dopamine levels, together with decreased γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA), indicating broader neurotransmitter alterations. These findings show that chronic PS-MPs exposure is associated with widespread brain metabolic perturbations, mitochondrial dysfunction, and dopaminergic impairment, highlighting associations between chronic PS-MPs exposure, brain metabolic alterations, and neurotoxic outcomes.

papers.title: The impact of acute sleep restriction on executive functions: A quasi-experimental within-subjects examination of inhibitory control, working memory, and cognitive flexibility.
papers.abstract: Acute sleep restriction can affect several aspects of higher-order cognition, including executive functioning. The present study examined how one night of acute sleep restriction affected three core components of executive functioning-inhibitory control, working memory, and cognitive flexibility-using a within-subjects experimental design. Thirty-three healthy adults aged 18-35 years completed a standardized neurocognitive battery consisting of the Stroop Color-Word Task, Go/No-Go Task, N-Back Task, Task-Switching Paradigm, and Wisconsin Card Sorting Test under two counterbalanced conditions: normal sleep (7-9 hours) and acute sleep restriction (≤4 hours). Sleep duration was monitored objectively using wrist actigraphy and supplemented with standardized sleep diaries. Performance declined across all three executive-function components following sleep restriction. The largest effects were observed in measures of cognitive flexibility, including increased switch costs and perseverative errors. Overall, the findings suggest that even a single night of substantial sleep restriction can adversely affect executive functioning, with cognitive flexibility appearing particularly sensitive to reduced sleep.

papers.title: Hair-compatible adhesive hydrogel electrodes for electroencephalography-based cybersickness detection and closed-loop mitigation.
papers.abstract: Cybersickness develops dynamically during virtual reality (VR) exposure, creating a need for continuous electroencephalography (EEG) monitoring. However, wearable EEG remains limited by the difficulty of establishing low-impedance, conformal, and mechanically stable electrode-scalp interfaces on hair-covered skin, especially under sweating and head motion. Here, we report a shell-assisted adhesive hydrogel electrode that combines hair penetration with stable scalp adhesion for rapid EEG acquisition. Poly (3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene)-modified polydopamine particles (PDA/PEDOT) are incorporated into an adhesive hydrogel to achieve high conductivity, strong adhesion, and mechanical compliance while preserving PEDOT conductivity without poly (styrene sulfonate) incorporation or additional treatment. A flexible silicone shell guides the hydrogel through hair, prevents unwanted hydrogel-hair adhesion, and enables intimate scalp contact. The electrode achieves an EEG signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 11.66 dB, while motion-induced interference under sweating is only 22.8% of that observed with traditional wet electrodes. Integrated into a wearable headband, the system detects cybersickness with 92.5% accuracy and enables closed-loop noisy galvanic vestibular stimulation (nGVS), increasing users' tolerance time by 52.3%. This work provides a practical strategy for hair-compatible soft biointerfaces and wearable neurotechnology for immersive human-machine interaction.

papers.title: Life stage-specific endocrine disruption by Tris(2-ethylhexyl) trimellitate (TOTM) in zebrafish: Thyroid-neurobehavioral effects and metabolic-reproductive alterations.
papers.abstract: Tris(2-ethylhexyl) trimellitate (TOTM) is a widely used plasticizer alternative to bis(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate in medical and consumer products, yet its toxicological profile remains poorly characterized. Given the increasing detection of TOTM in environmental matrices, concerns regarding its potential biological activity are rising. This study evaluated the endocrine-disrupting potential of TOTM across zebrafish life stages, integrating apical endpoints with transcriptomic profiling to investigate potential mechanisms. In 7 days post-fertilization (dpf) larvae, TOTM exposure produced a hyperthyroid-like hormone profile, with elevated whole-body thyroid hormones accompanied by altered transcription of thyroid axis-related genes, including some responses in the lowest exposure group (<0.047 mg/L). This hormonal imbalance was accompanied by significant hypoactivity in the light-dark transition assay, with reductions in total distance moved, mean velocity, and acceleration observed during the second light cycle. Transcriptomic analysis at 5.00 mg/L revealed that these neurobehavioral alterations were potentially linked to disrupted phototransduction and circadian rhythm pathways. In contrast, adult male zebrafish exposed to TOTM exhibited distinct metabolic and reproductive toxicity. While thyroid hormones showed no significant changes, reduced hepatic total cholesterol and sex steroid imbalance were observed at < 0.047 and 0.38 mg/L. These changes were supported by transcriptional alterations in steroidogenic and lipid metabolism genes. Collectively, the current findings demonstrate that TOTM exposure disrupts endocrine function, with different susceptibility by life stage in zebrafish: primarily targeting the thyroid-neurobehavioral axis in developing larvae while disrupting lipid and sex steroid homeostasis in adults. These results highlight the complex endocrine-disruption profile of TOTM and underscore the need for subsequent observational studies in human populations.

papers.title: Co-exposure to octocrylene and polystyrene nanoplastics induces neuro- and reproductive toxicity in zebrafish: Association with circadian rhythm and HPG axis disruption.
papers.abstract: Octocrylene (OC) is a widely used ultraviolet filter frequently detected in aquatic environments. Micro- and nanoplastics (M/NPs) are persistent pollutants that can adsorb organic contaminants such as OC, leading to combined exposure risks. However, the long-term neuroendocrine effects of environmentally relevant co-exposure to OC and nanoplastics remain poorly understood. In this study, adult zebrafish were exposed to OC (5 µg/L) with or without polystyrene nanoplastics (PS-NPs, 80 nm, 1.0 mg/L) for 28 days. Co-exposure to OC and PS-NPs significantly disrupted behavioral phenotypes, suppressed bdnf transcription, and downregulated core circadian clock genes (per1b, per2, per3, cry1a, cry2, nr1d1), indicating aggravated neurotoxicity. Furthermore, co-exposure interfered with sex hormone synthesis and caused gonadal damage by modulating the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal (HPG) axis at the transcriptional level, leading to more severe reproductive toxicity and impaired offspring development. Molecular docking revealed that OC may directly interact with estrogen receptors (ERα, ERβ) and CYP19, providing a molecular basis for endocrine disruption. These findings demonstrate that PS-NPs enhance the neurotoxic and reproductive effects of OC through circadian and HPG axis disruption, highlighting the need for considering nanoplastics as toxicity amplifiers in environmental risk assessment.

papers.title: Sense of coherence and health-related outcomes in medical cannabis patients with chronic pain: A cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: This study examined the relationship between Sense of Coherence (SOC) and health-related variables in individuals with chronic pain using medical cannabis. This cross-sectional, exploratory study employed correlational and group comparison analyses. A total of 156 patients treated through five Brazilian cannabis social organizations completed an online survey. Measures included a sociodemographic questionnaire, SOC-13 Scale, Brief Pain Inventory, Depression Anxiety Stress Scale-21 (DASS-21), Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) and World Health Organization Quality of Life Brief Scale (WHOQOL-BREF). Most participants were white, middle-aged women using THC-rich cannabis oil for more than six months. The mean SOC score was 52.64 (SD = 12.40). Mean pain intensity was mild (M = 3.99, SD = 2.60), while pain interference was moderate (M = 4.48, SD = 3.16). Participants reported moderate levels of depression (M = 13.82, SD = 12.04), and anxiety (M = 10.30, SD = 9.72), and mild stress (M = 16.28, SD = 11.32). Quality of life was rated low in the physical domain (M = 2.91, SD = 0.82) and regular in the others. Exploratory comparisons between participants with strong versus weak SOC indicated that stronger SOC was associated with lower levels of depression (p < 0.001, r = 0.6) and reduced pain interference (p < 0.001, r = 0.4). Among patients using medical cannabis, stronger SOC was associated with better health-related outcomes, particularly in mental health domains, even in the context of chronic stressors such as chronic pain. These findings highlight the potential relevance of salutogenic resources in contexts of chronic stress and illness.

papers.title: Utilizing wearable activity trackers to promote physical activity in people with epilepsy: a randomized controlled trial.
papers.abstract: To evaluate exercise education alone versus exercise education in combination with a wearable physical activity tracker in people with epilepsy (PWE) to determine the effect on physical activity and measure potential impact on depression, anxiety, sleep, and quality of life (QoL). In an open parallel group prospective randomized controlled trial, PWE between 18 and 64 years old were recruited from a single US epilepsy center. Eligible participants were randomized into two groups (control and intervention arms). Both arms received standard-of-care exercise education for PWE. The intervention arm also received a Fitbit for data monitoring and smartphone-application-based physical activity challenge opportunities. Both arms provided self-reported physical activity metrics at enrollment and study completion. Fitbit data were collected from each participant in the intervention arm continuously for three months. Secondary outcome measures for depression, anxiety, sleep, and QoL were also assessed at baseline and post-intervention. Seizure frequency was monitored as an adverse event. Eighty participants were recruited (40 intervention, 40 control). There was a significant increase in aerobic physical activity level after three months within the intervention arm and a nonsignificant positive trend within the control arm. There was a nonsignificant improvement in depression and anxiety scores in both arms. There was no significant change in sleep or QoL and no adverse impact on seizure frequency. The use of wearable physical activity trackers in conjunction with smartphone-application-based physical activity challenges and exercise education resulted in a within-intervention-arm improvement in aerobic physical activity in PWE with no change in seizure frequency.

papers.title: Almond shells as environmental enrichment for laying hens: Implications for welfare and egg quality.
papers.abstract: Environmental enrichment is a promising strategy to improve welfare in laying hens, particularly in aviary systems where large group sizes and complex social interactions can predispose birds to fearfulness and feather pecking. This study evaluated the effects of providing coarsely milled almond shells (AS; geometric mean diameter = 1525 µm) as an environmental enrichment on welfare indicators, egg quality, and organ development in large commercial aviary flocks. The study compared two treatments-hens receiving AS and a control group that did not receive AS-with four pens per treatment and 2,500 hens per pen. Welfare indicators, as well as external and internal egg quality traits, were assessed at peak lay (13 weeks (wk) of trial; 33 weeks of age) and post-peak lay (23 wk of trial; 43 wk of age). In addition, at 23 wk of trial, serum corticosterone and relative organ weights were measured. At peak lay, hens provided with AS enrichment showed reduced fearfulness in the novel object test (P < 0.001), a trend toward lower gentle feather pecking (P < 0.1), and fewer comb pecking wounds and lower overall pecking scores (P < 0.001). No differences were observed in free feathers in the litter or severe/aggressive pecking. At post-peak, hens provided with AS enrichment continued to show lower fear responses (P < 0.001), fewer free feathers in the litter (P < 0.05), and tendencies toward reduced plumage damage, lower overall pecking scores, and reduced serum corticosterone (7.05 vs. 11.23 ng/mL; P < 0.1). Both internal and external egg quality parameters remained unaffected at both ages. Relative weights of liver, proventriculus, gizzard, pancreas, and spleen were unchanged, while small and large intestines tended to be heavier in hens provided with AS enrichment (P < 0.1). In conclusion, milled AS could be an effective enrichment for aviary-housed laying hens, by reducing fear and stress, mitigating feather pecking, and supporting minor digestive adaptations, without compromising egg quality. These findings support the use of AS as a sustainable agricultural by-product to improve welfare in large commercial flocks.

papers.title: Associations of circadian clock genes with the risk of depression in adults with sleep disturbances: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Depression, influenced by both genetic and environmental factors, is often accompanied by sleep disturbances. However, studies examining the associations between circadian clock genes, depression, and sleep disturbances have yielded inconsistent findings. This study investigated the associations of circadian clock genes with depression in adults with sleep disturbances. A systematic search of six databases (EBSCOhost, Medline, Scopus, Embase, PubMed, and Web of Science) was conducted for articles published up to July 10, 2025. The study was registered with PROSPERO (CRD42023472328). A total of 23 studies examining depression in adults with sleep disturbances were included. Eight genes (CLOCK, NR1D, TIM, CRY, PER2, PER3, ARNTL, and CSNK1) were associated with depression in adults with sleep disturbances, while RORA showed no significant association. CRY showed the numerically highest pooled odds ratio for depression in adults with sleep disturbances (OR= 1.6, 95% CI: 1.4-1.8, p < 0.01), although its confidence interval overlapped with those of several other genes. These findings underscore the role of circadian genes and suggest further gene identification may clarify depression and sleep disturbance pathways.

papers.title: Automated attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder detection using an explainable EEGNet model based on electroencephalogram signals.
papers.abstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition where traditional diagnostics often suffer from subjective biases and a lack of objective biomarkers. In this study, we developed a novel, automated, and interpretable diagnostic framework using the specialized EEGNet model to extract spatio-temporal patterns directly from raw EEG signals, ensuring robust ADHD detection and model generalizability across a clinical lifespan ranging from 5 to 89 years. The primary innovation of this research lies in a specialized, lightweight EEGNet model that directly processes raw 5-second spatio-temporal EEG segments, eliminating the need for manual feature engineering or signal-to-image transformation. Our findings demonstrate that EEGNet achieves superior performance, reaching an average accuracy of 89.48% (±4.21%) and an AUC of 0.96 (±0.03), significantly outperforming the transfer learning models. A distinguishing feature of this work is the transition from black-box modeling to explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) by integrating Saliency Maps and SHAP values, which decoded the model's decision-making logic to identify key contributing channels (Fp1, Fp2, C3, T5, and A2) whose spatial attributions align with established neuroscientific literature on ADHD. The high ranking of the Fp1 (prefrontal) channel aligns with established neuroscientific evidence regarding executive dysfunction in ADHD. Furthermore, the implementation of a rigorous inter-subject evaluation demonstrates the preliminary clinical feasibility of this interpretable framework, providing a foundation for future validation on larger multi-center cohorts and offering a robust assistive tool for real-world neurological assessments.

papers.title: Poor R-wave progression and long-term outcomes in the multi-ethnic study of atherosclerosis (MESA).
papers.abstract: Poor R-wave progression (PRWP) has been interpreted as a marker of anterior myocardial injury since the 1970s, but its temporal stability, substrate, and independent prognostic value in a CAD-free cohort remain uncertain. We studied 6323 MESA participants free of clinical cardiovascular disease with standardized 12‑lead ECGs at baseline (Exam 1, 2000-02) and after a median of 10 years (Exam 5, 2010-12). PRWP was defined as R-wave amplitude ≤3 mm in V3 with RV3 > RV2. We assessed 10-year test-retest stability (Cohen's κ), pulmonary/thoracic correlates, mechanistic substrate via cardiac magnetic resonance, high-sensitivity troponin T, NT-proBNP, and polysomnography, and long-term outcomes (all-cause death, cardiovascular death, MACE) over median 14 years using Cox and Fine-Gray models. PRWP prevalence was 3.2% at Exam 1 and 6.2% at Exam 5. Binary test-retest agreement was limited (κ = 0.344; 95% CI 0.283-0.406) despite good continuous R-V3 reliability (ICC = 0.73); only 52% of baseline PRWP persisted at 10 years. Self-reported emphysema (OR 4.48; 2.30-8.22) and current smoking (OR 1.77; 1.14-2.73) were the strongest PRWP predictors. PRWP was not associated with RV volumes, RV ejection fraction, NT-proBNP, or sleep apnea. After adjustment for smoking and emphysema, PRWP was not independently associated with all-cause mortality (HR 1.19; 0.90-1.58), cardiovascular death (HR 1.02; 0.67-1.57), or MACE (HR 0.89; 0.54-1.47). Time-updated and Fine-Gray models confirmed null associations. In a CAD-free multi-ethnic cohort, isolated PRWP is an ECG pattern with limited binary reproducibility, linked to pulmonary exposure and thoracic habitus rather than myocardial substrate, and carries no independent cardiovascular prognostic value.

papers.title: Prevalence and clinical correlates of sleep disturbances in hemifacial spasm: A multi-centre case-control study.
papers.abstract: Hemifacial spasm (HFS) is a chronic movement disorder characterised by involuntary contractions of muscles on one side of the face. While motor features are well recognised, sleep disturbances in HFS have not been studied in detail. We aimed to compare the prevalence of sleep disturbances between HFS patients and healthy controls and examine clinical factors associated with sleep dysfunction in HFS. This cross-sectional case-control study included 133 HFS patients and 227 age- and gender-matched healthy controls. Validated questionnaires were used to assess excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS), sleep quality, insomnia, restless legs syndrome (RLS), probable rapid eye movement sleep behaviour disorder (pRBD), and high risk of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). Anxiety, depression, and quality of life were assessed. HFS severity was assessed using the Hemifacial Spasm Grading Scale. Compared to healthy controls, HFS patients had a greater prevalence of EDS (P = 0.003), poor sleep quality (P < 0.001), moderate-to-severe insomnia (P < 0.001), pRBD (P = 0.007), RLS (P < 0.001), high risk for OSA (P = 0.005), depression (P = 0.009), and lower quality of life (P < 0.001). Multivariate analysis showed that poor sleep quality was associated with anxiety; RLS with HFS severity, and high risk for OSA with a higher body mass index (BMI) and hypertension, among patients with HFS. Poor quality of life in HFS was associated with presence of poor sleep quality, pRBD, RLS, anxiety, and depressive symptoms. Sleep disturbances are common in HFS, and are associated with disease severity, high BMI, and anxiety. Sleep and mood symptoms worsen quality of life in these patients.

papers.title: The effects of aromatherapy and music listening on sleep and cerebral oxygen levels in children with epilepsy.
papers.abstract: This study compared aromatherapy and music listening with routine care regarding sleep parameters and cerebral oxygenation in children with epilepsy. This three-arm, parallel-group randomized controlled trial was conducted between February and December 2023. Ninety-six children with epilepsy were randomized to aromatherapy, music listening, or control (32 per group), and ninety were included in the per-protocol analyses (30 per group). Interventions were delivered at home during a single evening. Sleep was assessed using 24-h actigraphy, and regional cerebral oxygen saturation (rSO2) was monitored for 150 min. Data were collected using the Patient Introduction and Follow-up Form, actigraphy, and the Cerebral Oxygen Monitoring Form. One-way ANOVA, Kruskal-Wallis, chi-square, Mann-Whitney U, LSD, Dunnett's C, and ANCOVA were used. Both interventions were associated with longer sleep duration, higher sleep efficiency, shorter sleep-onset latency, and higher rSO2 than routine care (p < 0.05). Aromatherapy was also associated with longer time in bed than routine care and longer sleep duration than music listening. Wake after sleep onset and nighttime awakenings did not differ significantly among groups. Both interventions were associated with favorable short-term sleep outcomes and higher rSO2. The clinical significance and persistence of these findings remain uncertain. These preliminary findings support further evaluation of brief bedtime interventions in pediatric epilepsy nursing, with family education, respect for children's willingness to participate, and monitoring. Retrospectively registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT07827729; first posted September 11, 2026).

papers.title: The observer's blind spot: Discrepancies between self-reported and external ratings of dream affect.
papers.abstract: Because dream experiences are largely accessible only through retrospective reports after awakening, estimates of dream affect may depend on who evaluates the report. We compared dreamers' self-ratings with ratings made by independent external judges to examine how rating method influences estimates of the presence, valence, and intensity of dream affect. The dataset comprised 1,946 home dream reports from 106 adults; models that included age used data from 104 participants. Dreams were judged as significantly more affective and emotionally intense when self-rated than when evaluated by external judges. External judges classified fewer dreams as containing affect and fewer dreams as positively valenced than did self-ratings. A three-way interaction among rating method, valence, and participants' biological sex indicated that biological sex influenced self-ratings but not external ones: women reported more intense negative dreams than men, whereas men rated their negative dreams as less intense than their own positive dreams; these differences disappeared when external ratings were used. While word count positively predicted affective occurrence and intensity, it did not account for valence. Self- and external ratings showed a significant positive association, although agreement at the level of individual dream reports was modest. Agreement was higher for negative than positive classifications. These results indicate that rating methods shape empirical portraits of dream affect and that self- and external ratings capture overlapping but noninterchangeable aspects of remembered dream experience.

papers.title: Racial/Ethnic Variations in the Association Between Sleep Problems and Mental Health.
papers.abstract: Racial/ethnic disparities in mental health remain a pressing concern in social work, yet limited research has explored whether commonly experienced stressors differentially affect mental health outcomes across racial/ethnic groups. This study investigated whether race/ethnicity moderates the association between sleep problems and mental health. Data were drawn from the 2022 National Health Interview Survey (N = 25,225). Depressive symptoms were assessed using the eight-item Patient Health Questionnaire, and anxiety symptoms were measured using the seven-item Generalized Anxiety Disorder scale. Sleep problems were evaluated across four dimensions: (1) waking up feeling unrested, (2) difficulty falling asleep, (3) difficulty staying asleep, and (4) use of sleep medication. Race/ethnicity was categorized as non-Hispanic White, Hispanic, Black, and Asian. Results indicated that sleep problems were associated with higher levels of depressive and anxiety symptoms. The positive association between sleep problems and both outcomes was stronger among Hispanic adults compared with non-Hispanic White adults. These differences persisted across several sleep dimensions, including difficulty falling asleep, difficulty staying asleep, and use of sleep medication. Patterns among Black and Asian adults were more varied. These findings underscore the need for social work research and practice to incorporate sleep health into broader efforts to address racial/ethnic mental health disparities.

papers.title: Sleep disturbance in inflammatory bowel disease: clinical associations and gaps in care.
papers.abstract: Sleep disturbance is highly prevalent in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), affecting up to 70% of patients with active disease and 40% in remission, and is associated with worse clinical and patient-reported outcomes. Understanding of the multifactorial drivers of sleep disturbances in IBD remains limited, and as such, there is an absence of clear guidance for evaluating and managing sleep problems in this population. We aimed to identify factors associated with sleep disturbance and characterize patient beliefs, self-management strategies, and interest in sleep-focused testing and treatments. Adults with Crohn disease and ulcerative colitis completed a cross-sectional survey assessing disease activity, sleep quality, stress, chronotype, fatigue, and mood. A study-specific questionnaire evaluated sleep-related beliefs, behaviors, and treatment interest. Descriptive analyses characterized sleep patterns and behaviors, and multivariable regression identified factors associated with poor sleep. Among 204 participants, 76.5% reported poor sleep quality and 55.9% had clinically significant sleep disturbance, which was more common in active disease than remission (80.9% vs 46.0%, P < .001). Active disease (odds ratio [OR], 4.31), higher perceived stress (OR, 1.21), and anxiety (OR, 2.63) were associated with increased odds of clinically significant sleep disturbance, while intermediate (OR, 0.16) and morning chronotypes (OR, 0.07) were associated with lower odds of clinically significant sleep disturbance compared with evening chronotypes. Most participants reported self-management behaviors related to sleep, with widespread use of sleep hygiene and over-the-counter strategies but minimal exposure to cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (0.5%). Interest in sleep-focused interventions was high, particularly for wearable monitoring, home-based testing, and behavioral and light-based therapies. Sleep disturbance in inflammatory bowel disease is common and reflects interacting inflammatory, psychological, and circadian factors. Use of evidence-based therapies remains extremely limited, highlighting a substantial gap in care.

papers.title: Preoperative Sleep Modulation with Melatonin and Zolpidem and Its Impact on Postoperative Pain and Recovery: A Scoping Review.
papers.abstract: Perioperative sleep disturbances and anxiety may worsen postoperative pain, increase opioid consumption, and delay recovery. Melatonin and zolpidem improve sleep, but their effects on postoperative pain remain incompletely characterized. PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched for studies published between 2000 and 2025 investigating preoperative melatonin or zolpidem in surgical patients. Two reviewers independently screened records using Rayyan, resolving discrepancies through consensus. Of 404 records identified, 119 duplicates were removed. Of 285 screened records, 269 were excluded, leaving 16 articles for inclusion. Melatonin demonstrated anxiolytic, analgesic, and chronobiotic effects. It reduced salivary cortisol, modulated stress responses, attenuated proinflammatory pathways, and supported circadian recovery, particularly in patients with preoperative anxiety. Its analgesic efficacy was comparable to clonidine in some trials, with a favorable safety profile. Zolpidem improved preoperative sleep quality and reduced postoperative pain and opioid consumption, potentially through improved sleep architecture. In colorectal surgery, zolpidem also reduced tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α). Melatonin demonstrated more consistent effects on cortisol, suggesting distinct physiological mechanisms. Melatonin and zolpidem offer complementary perioperative benefits. Melatonin may provide broader neuroendocrine and analgesic effects, whereas zolpidem may benefit patients with insomnia. Larger trials are needed to optimize dosing and patient selection.
papers.journal: Journal of pain & palliative care pharmacotherapy

papers.title: Metabolic Imaging of Optic Nerve Oligodendrocytes Following AAV-Mediated Sensor Delivery.
papers.abstract: Oligodendrocytes are key regulators of white matter integrity, supporting rapid nerve conduction and sustaining axonal health. They engage in metabolic interactions with axons, yet their metabolic dynamics and specializations remain difficult to study in intact tissue. The optic nerve provides an accessible and well-structured white matter tract in which oligodendrocytes maintain their native association with axons and surrounding glia. Here, we present a protocol for targeted biosensor expression in oligodendrocytes of the optic nerve using intracerebroventricular injection of adeno-associated viruses (AAVs) at postnatal day 10 (P10). This approach enables imaging of oligodendrocyte metabolism in an intact 3D environment. As a use case, we demonstrate expression and application of a genetically encoded glucose sensor, allowing metabolic imaging to be combined with functional assays such as optic nerve electrophysiology. This method provides a flexible platform for studying oligodendrocyte physiology and metabolic adaptation in health and disease.

papers.title: Measuring Conduction Velocity by Compound Action Potential (CAP) Recordings.
papers.abstract: The recording of compound action potentials (CAPs)-the summed activity of multiple axons-is a reliable method for calculating the average conduction velocity of a population of axons. This chapter presents a detailed overview of how CAP recordings can be used to quantify action potential conduction velocity in acute brain slices of the adult mouse brain. We describe a step-by-step protocol for recording CAPs in the medial corpus callosum, highlighting technical considerations that improve data quality and reproducibility. Methods for analyzing CAP waveforms are discussed, including strategies to distinguish between fast-conducting myelinated fibers and slower unmyelinated populations. By providing practical guidance on experimental design, execution, and analysis, this chapter underscores the enduring value of CAP recordings as a versatile tool for probing axonal conduction and advancing our understanding of central nervous system function in health and disease.

papers.title: Age-dependent association of body mass index and obstructive sleep apnea severity in women.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is influenced by body mass index (BMI), age, and sex. Although obesity is a major risk factor for OSA, the strength of the association between BMI and OSA severity may vary across demographic groups. We investigated whether age modifies the relationship between BMI and OSA severity in men and women. We performed a cross-sectional analysis of adults who underwent polysomnography at a university-based sleep laboratory. The relationship between BMI and apnea-hypopnea index (AHI), including supine AHI, was evaluated. Participants were categorized into younger and older age groups (< 55 vs. ≥55 years). Linear regression models with interaction terms were used to assess whether age modified the association between BMI and OSA severity. A total of 752 participants were included. The associations of BMI categories with normalized AHI and normalized supine AHI were weaker in older women than in younger women (P for interaction = 0.03 and 0.02, respectively), whereas no significant interaction by age group was observed in men. Results were similar for log-transformed BMI (P for interaction = 0.03 for both in women). However, the three-way interaction among BMI, age group, and sex was not significant. The association between BMI and OSA severity was attenuated in women aged 55 years or older compared with younger women. Because a sex difference in this age-related attenuation was not statistically confirmed, these findings should be interpreted with caution. They suggest that BMI alone may be a less informative indicator of OSA severity in older women.

papers.title: How obstructive sleep apnea differs in COPD and asthma: insights from a clinical and functional study.
papers.abstract: Direct comparisons between Overlap Syndrome (OVS), the concomitance of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), and alternative Overlap Syndrome (aOVS), the concomitance of OSA with asthma, are limited. To describe clinical and respiratory differences between OVS and aOVS. This retrospective single-centre study included 66 patients with OVS and 35 patients with aOVS. All patients underwent Home Sleep Apnea test (HSAT) and spirometry. Predicted Low arousal threshold (LowAT) was estimated using validated predictive models based on HSAT criteria. Patients with OVS exhibited significantly higher Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI), oxygen desaturation index (ODI) and Time spent with SpO2 < 90% (T90%) compared to aOVS. aOVS was associated with significantly higher odds of night-time awakenings, insomnia symptoms and fatigue.
